body:
Thanks for the PR! I think this is a bit more complicated than it might seem at first glance.

I think that instead of the `@bitfield` annotation applicable to enums, we should have a separate static type `BitField[T]` (where `T` is an enum type). This type would only exist in the static analyzer; at runtime, it would simply be `int` (as is done for enum types). This way, you could distinguish between exporting a choice of one of the flags as a drop-down list (`@export var flag: MyFlagsEnum`) and exporting a choice of a combination of these flags (`@export var flag: BitField[MyFlagsEnum]`) as a list of checkboxes. That is, in the first case, only one value from the enum is allowed, while in the second, any combination of the bitwise OR of all the enum values ​​(including the empty value, `0`) is allowed. See also #100888.

Regarding the `@bitfield` annotation on enums, I'm not sure it's even necessary. In the core, the only difference between a regular enum and an enum marked as `is_bitfield` is in the docs: in the former, it's marked as `enum`, in the latter as `flags`. Also, I don't think restricting the allowed values ​​or changing the autoincrement behavior for values ​​in powers of two is a good idea. Users often want a `NONE = 0` element or elements that are combinations of multiple flags. In these cases, there's no obvious solution for how the language should behave if the user specifies an unexpected flag value. In my opinion, giving flag enums any special behavior is pointless. It's better to let users explicitly specify the values ​​in powers of two (you can use the bitwise shift operator).

See also #100888.

The main reason I had for making a `@bitfield` annotation is that using the `[Flags]` attribute on an enum in C# has the same effects as this PR, making behavior match (although behavior-match isn't too important between C# and GDScript, but it's always nice).

Having the choice between having the flags as a drop-down or a combination with `BitField[T]` does sound nice, as that was one of the main concerns I had while making this, it restricts all exported usages of the bitfield enum to having a combination of flags.

~~Another problem that would rise is that, unless I'm misunderstanding something with it being analyzer-only, it would essentially be a nested type when used with a typed dictionary or array, which is currently not supported at all in GDScript.~~ I did misunderstand, since they're analyzer only, they can be nested.

In general though, I am pretty favorable to having `BitField[T]`, if I were to go ahead with that, would I have to open another PR that supersedes this one and leaving this one open while waiting for the new PR to be merged, or is there another procedure ?

It's better to let users explicitly specify the values ​​in powers of two (you can use the bitwise shift operator).

Auto-increment behavior was mentioned in the proposal, but in hindsight there are a couple of issues, which you mentioned. Even the `[Flags]` attribute in C#, which this PR is _slightly_ based on, doesn't seem to auto-initialize values to `2^n`. The documentation changing `enum` to `flags` is not even noticeable, especially since it doesn't have a tooltip like `BitField[T]` in the documentation, so losing that is insignificant.

I have the `BitField[T]` implementation ready, just need clarification on what I should do with this PR. Should I make a new one for the new implementation and keep this one open ? Should this one get closed ? Should there even be a new PR ?

> Should I make a new one for the new implementation and keep this one open ?

You can do it however you prefer. If you agree that the new approach is better, you can update this PR (including the title and description). Otherwise, you can open a new one so we have two alternatives to compare.
Even though I do think the new implementation is better, a new PR has been opened at #117601 for easier comparison between the two.
